scope: Production-Chromium file-size scaling with stream-copy and genuine decode/re-encode kept as separate topologies
measurementFormula: peak complete Chromium process-tree private memory during conversion - stable private memory of the same clean Chromium instance on a blank page before the converter is loaded

genuineReencode.classificationProof: The input video codec is HEVC and the independently probed output video codec is VP8; changing that elementary bitstream requires decode and encode, not an extension change or container-only remux.
genuineReencode.sourceLineage: Both inputs are valid Matroska media from the protected source; the small point is a native stream-copy fixture used only as browser-converter input and the large point is the untouched protected file.

scaling.finding: Input grew 78.98x and output grew 129.67x while worst complete-Chromium incremental private memory grew only 1.34x and remained 41.20 MiB below the hard limit. This is strongly sublinear and consistent with bounded I/O rather than whole-file retention.

streamCopyRemux.classificationProof: Independent probes report HEVC video and AAC audio before and after; packets are copied into MP4 without decode/re-encode. The 92-second 10 GB result is therefore plausible I/O-bound remuxing and is not claimed as transcoding.

scaling.finding: Input and output each grew 1.67x while memory grew 1.08x. Throughput remained within 0.7%, and both complete-process-tree results stayed below 250 MiB.

independentValidation.nativeToolsRole: fixture preparation plus post-conversion FFprobe, packet traversal, full output byte count, and SHA-256 only

limitations: The genuine re-encode scaling reports were recorded on Chrome 150 and the remux scaling reports on Chrome 151; current Chrome 152 route correctness and per-profile memory remain covered separately.
The 120-second re-encode point has one passing run, while the full 2.958 GB point has the required three repeatable runs.
The raw timestamped reports are intentionally repository-local and ignored because they contain bulky process samples; their exact hashes and compact results are retained here.
This audit proves representative topology scaling, not that every one of the 388 public profiles has been tested at multi-gigabyte scale.
